extraction_grammar.result_initializer_form: one const result object literal with unquoted identifier keys followed by colons
extraction_grammar.dynamic_result_field_form: line-leading direct result.identifier = value for new fields; declared fields also permit the established += counter update
extraction_grammar.result_assignment_target_form: delete, prefix/postfix update, for-of, for-in, parenthesized, computed, destructured, whole-result, aliased, helper, and indirect targets are refused; only the declared direct-property and collection-mutation forms may write result
extraction_grammar.call_identifier_form: unescaped double-quoted literal first arguments for record, runPhase, timing.start, timing.duration, timing.milestone, and recordLongWait
extraction_grammar.sensitive_reference_form: record, runPhase, and recordLongWait permit only their exact canonical declarations and canonical direct calls; timing permits its exact declaration, canonical direct tracked-method calls, the declared timing.duration(kind, ...) forwarder, and the exact timing.summary() result projection; aliases, value capture, indirect invocation, optional/computed access, call/apply/bind, and reassignment fail
extraction_grammar.validation_scope_form: one inline double-quoted literal array followed by .includes(VALIDATION_SCOPE)

thin_golden_path.duplication_justification: The golden child repeats only one happy-case signal from each referenced owner to prove composition. It excludes naming/activation matrices, approval/cancel/resume, full decision/Transition, portability/restart, responsive matrices, and failure combinations.

changed_file_selection: Map changed files to repository-owned detailed owner sets.
Fail closed to all Browser shards when ownership is ambiguous, shared runtime/process/authority code changes, inventory/contract changes invalidate the map, or multiple owner boundaries are touched.
Require the thin golden path whenever a selected change can affect composition across two or more detailed owners or the shared fixture/harness boundary.
Require all Browser shards for full mode and for shared fixture, runtime, process lifecycle, Browser harness, authority, planner, executor, or receipt changes.
selected_shard_result_requirements: zero listener, DB, profile, and temporary-root residue
planner_receipt_design.aggregation_rule: All planner-selected shards and any mandatory golden path must pass before the aggregated exact-head receipt is deciding. A missing, skipped, failed, timed-out, stale, or cleanup-incomplete required shard makes the receipt non-deciding.
planner_receipt_design.focused_vs_deciding: A focused shard result is attributable diagnostic evidence for one owner. It is not the aggregated deciding receipt unless the exact planner selected only that owner and every other required invariant/golden result is present.
planner_receipt_design.timing_attribution: Receipt material retains phase, cleanup, stream-settlement, and total duration per owner before computing aggregate duration.

rules: Define semantic responsibility before selecting a timeout.
Measure phase execution, cleanup, and stream-settlement distributions separately per owner.
Retain meaningful normal-operation headroom rather than steady-state execution near the child bound.
Treat timeout as failure containment, not expected successful termination.
Do not split by equal elapsed halves.
Do not add pass-chasing retries, arbitrary sleeps, assertion weakening, or automatic timeout widening.

sequencing.responsibility: Inventory, ownership, dependencies, fixture boundary, golden specification, and static completeness contracts.
Extract independent operator and execution shard.
Wire planner selection, thin golden path, per-shard receipt material, aggregation, and old-owner removal after equivalence proof.

non_goals: No operator-execution, golden-path, or additional Browser shard extraction.
No legacy Browser assertion, scope, execution ordering, timeout, retry, or sleep change.
No deletion or shortening of e2e-core.
No Local Canonical planner selection or receipt deciding-semantics change.
No product, UI, API, schema, Core, protocol, native-host, authority, or runtime behavior change.
No VFY1-C, VFY1-D, C9, or PC6 implementation.
